sources.entry: statsmodels - Statistical modeling and econometrics in Python.

summary.one_liner: statsmodels is a Python package that complements scipy with descriptive statistics and estimation and inference for statistical models.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes statsmodels as a complement to scipy for statistical computations, covering descriptive statistics and estimation and inference for statistical models. Listed model families include linear regression (OLS, GLS, WLS, quantile, recursive least squares), mixed linear models, GLM, GEE, discrete models (Logit, Probit, MNLogit, Poisson, negative binomial, zero-inflated), and robust linear models (RLM). It also includes time series tools (ARIMA, VAR/VECM, state space, Markov switching, exponential smoothing, unit root and cointegration tests), survival analysis (Cox, Kaplan-Meier), multivariate methods (PCA, factor analysis, MANOVA, canonical correlation), kernel density estimation, a wide range of statistical tests, MICE imputation, and mediation analysis. Plotting functions and table output to ASCII, LaTeX, and HTML are also mentioned.
use_cases: fit ordinary least squares or regression models in Python
analyze time series with ARIMA or VAR
survival analysis with Cox models or Kaplan-Meier curves
run statistical hypothesis tests and diagnostics
how_to_run: python -m pip install -i statsmodels --upgrade --use-deprecated=legacy-resolver (nightly wheel, per README)
See INSTALL.txt for building from sources
notable: Broad coverage from regression and GLM to state space time series and survival analysis
Sandbox folder holds experimental code such as GMM, kernel regression, and panel data models
Table output to ASCII, LaTeX, and HTML
caveats: Sandbox code is not considered production ready
Pandas has a more recent version of the Stata .dta reader, per README
Building from source requires following INSTALL.txt requirements
keywords: fit a regression model in python
